description:
World::function_definition (src/compiler2/world.rs:1804) returns (FunctionSource, FunctionSurface) built with `(*source.clone(), *surface.clone())`: a deep copy of both on every call. World::function_surface (world.rs:1813) calls it and discards the source it just copied.

Evidence (develop @ cca160808): 29 production call sites. Many read one Copy field and drop the rest:
- `.0.owner` only: dump.rs:240, :244; fixture_facts.rs:42, :45; jobs/semantic.rs:1494, :1670, :1686
- `.1.is_macro` only: compiler.rs:551
- `function_surface(..)` for .extern_abi, .clauses.len(), .span or a label: world.rs:1489; drive_harness.rs:1152; jobs/dispatch.rs:583, :585, :591, :603, :687, :701
- destructuring callers that then hold &mut World: jobs/body.rs:305 (lower_function), jobs/contract.rs:40, jobs/dispatch.rs:113, :244, :299, jobs/semantic.rs:2084, :2102, jobs/root.rs:53, world.rs:1050, :3574

Change: both accessors return borrows (`(&FunctionSource, &FunctionSurface)` and `&FunctionSurface`). Same method as fz-gfx.1: signature first, cargo check enumerates, sort callers into pure appeasement and real interleaving.

Expected knot: the job bodies (lower_function and its peers) read the definition and then run with &mut World, so they are real interleaving and will keep a visible clone at the call site under moves (a)/(b). A definition is immutable once defined (FunctionState::Defined), which is the case move (c) exists for; World::lowered_body already hands out Rc<LoweredBody> on the same grounds. Before building: count how many callers remain interleaving after (a)/(b). If it is most of the job bodies, stop and report -- storing the definition behind Rc is a data-model decision for the owner.

Found while building fz-gfx.2.

Signal: gate green, no golden/census/pin movement.
title: World hands out function definitions by reference
